title: Covert Mideast Oil Flows Are Keeping Global Prices in Check
summary:
(Bloomberg) -- Middle Eastern oil producers are pressing ahead with shuttling large volumes of crude out of the Persian Gulf, helping keep a lid on prices and assuaging fears of an energy-driven inflation spike, even as the Iran war drags on.
The incognito crossings of the world's most vital energy chokepoint have become a major lifeline for global markets that were bracing for a much worse supply shock when the Iran war broke out.
The volumes are running higher than market estimates of 4 million barrels a day, the people said, without specifying by how much.
Before the Iran war, about 20 million barrels a day crossed Hormuz, roughly a fifth of the world's oil supply.
That's far from the most alarming levels foreseen at the onset of the conflict if the Iran war lingered through the summer.

title: Iran says two French embassy employees barred from returning
summary:
DUBAI, Aug 17 (Reuters) - Iran said on Monday that two French embassy employees involved in ‌a diplomatic dispute last month would not be ‌allowed to return to Iran.

"Insisting that these individuals were engaged ‌in activities related ⁠to supporting civil society is itself an admission that the Vienna Convention was violated," ⁠Baghaei told a weekly press conference, without elaborating.
French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot, in an interview with France Inter last month, said the mission of the two ‌embassy employees concerned was to "develop programmes ​supporting Iranian civil society, students, ​and artists (...) France ​is one of the countries in ‌the world that does the ​most for Iranian ​civil society, and we have paid the price for it."

title: The post-Hormuz era offers Africa a great opportunity
summary:

title: Japan defence minister visits contentious Yasukuni Shrine to war dead
summary:
